name: Maryland Heights High School - Gymnasium
district_operator: Maryland Heights School District / Pattonville R-III (after 1962)
notes: FACILITY ROW, NOT A SCHOOL: this is the gymnasium of Maryland Heights High School (seed row ALL-163 in another batch) at 115 Harding Ave; no yearbook research should attach to it. District history confirms the gymnasium was built in 1951 for $40,000 and survived as the Pattonville printing facility after the main 1924 school building was demolished in 1998. Under Proposition S, the printing department moved to the renovated Holman Gym B (new Transportation Building/Print Shop completed ~June 2025), and the district states 'the current printing facility will be demolished and used for additional parking at [Pattonville] Heights' — consistent with the seed's 'demolished July 2025,' hence probable rather than confirmed on the exact date.

name: Carver School for Negroes
notes: Umbrella entity for the segregated Black elementary school operated by the Maryland Heights School District — the same school as campus rows ALL-166 (Adie Road) and ALL-167 (Harding Avenue); kept separate per no-silent-merge rule, but ALL-166+ALL-167 are the two physical sites of this single school. Pattonville's official district history confirms: at the 1962 merger the Maryland Heights district consisted of Maryland Heights High School, Remington Elementary, and 'Carver Elementary for Negroes,' and 'Carver was discontinued.' Opening date not found — the school predates the 1951 Harding Ave building (it replaced an earlier Adie Road building of unknown age). After 1962 the students were presumably absorbed into Pattonville elementaries (most plausibly Remington Elementary, ALL-151, nearby) but no source documents the receiving school. Recommended human follow-up: Missouri History Museum or St. Louis County Library African American schools holdings for the school's founding date; the St. Louis County Library Black Heritage Trail index references 'Carver Elementary School, Maryland Heights, Mo.' (pp. 73-74) in an unnamed source volume.

name: Carver School - Adie Road Campus
historical_names: Carver School for Negroes (Adie Road site)
notes: Earlier site of Carver School for Negroes (ALL-165): district history states Carver was 'formerly located at the end of Adie Road' and 'was replaced in 1951 with a new $15,000, two-room building on Harding Avenue near the Maryland Heights High School.' The school itself continued at ALL-167 — this row tracks the Adie Road building, which ceased use as the school in 1951. When the Adie Road facility itself was built could not be determined online.

name: Carver School - Harding Avenue Campus
historical_names: Carver Elementary School for Negroes (Harding Avenue site)
district_operator: Maryland Heights School District / Pattonville R-III (1962)
notes: Second (final) site of Carver School for Negroes (ALL-165): two-room building on Harding Avenue near the Maryland Heights High School, built 1951 for $15,000. Discontinued when the Maryland Heights School District merged into Pattonville R-3 in 1962 — the end of the segregated school. Receiving school(s) for Carver students after 1962 are not documented; Remington Elementary (ALL-151) is the geographic candidate. Seed's dates confirmed.

name: Penn School
notes: Seed's unknowns resolved by Pattonville's official history: a white-frame Penn School was erected circa 1850 on modern-day Creve Coeur Mill Road on Fee Fee Creek ('at about the same time the Fee Fee School opened' in 1850 — hence probable, not a documented exact year). A new brick Penn building opened in 1924. In 1936 Penn School and Junction School (ALL-169) merged to form Penn-Junction School (ALL-170); the Penn building was torn down. Mabel Brewster Remington (namesake of Remington Elementary) began teaching at Penn School in 1894.

name: Junction School
historical_names: Junction School (St. Charles Rock Road and Natural Bridge)
notes: Seed confirmed: opened 1869 — a white-frame one-room school seating 30 pupils at the St. Charles Rock Road and Natural Bridge intersection, across from the original Shumate Academy site (now the site of SSM DePaul Hospital). Merged with Penn School (ALL-168) in 1936 to form Penn-Junction School (ALL-170). Note the seed's '67' length field is junk (1869-1936 = 67 years is coincidental length arithmetic, not data).

name: Penn-Junction School
notes: Created by the 1936 Penn + Junction merger; located on Branneky Lane at McKelvey Road (later called Penn Junction Road). Seed's 'closed 1950' reflects the district annexation — Penn-Junction School District was annexed into Pattonville in May 1950, but the school itself kept operating as Penn-Junction Elementary under Pattonville (still one of five elementaries in 1956) until the 1982 district reorganization closed it effective the 1982-83 school year. The building reopened as the district's POSITIVE School (dropout-prevention program) and the board approved its sale to Grace World Outreach in May 1985. Students after 1982 were rezoned among remaining Pattonville elementaries; no single successor school.

name: Mount Pleasant School
district_operator: Mount Pleasant School District / Pattonville R-III (after 1951)
notes: Seed's 'closed 1951' reflects the district merger, not the school's end. Pattonville's official history: Mount Pleasant Schoolhouse was established in 1836 by Absolom Link east of the Fee Fee community (near modern Midland and Lindbergh); a new brick building went up in 1884 at 11050 N. Warson Road (the district history also says it 'later opened in 1889 as Mount Pleasant Elementary School,' an internal inconsistency — 1836 founding recorded as probable). The Mount Pleasant district merged with Pattonville in 1951, after which the school ran as Mount Pleasant Elementary until it was one of three schools closed in 1978 for declining enrollment. The building was sold to Christian Academy of Greater St. Louis in 1981. In 1965 Mount Pleasant Elementary was the first school west of the Mississippi to use closed-circuit television for instruction.

name: Pattonville Grade School
district_operator: Fee Fee District No. 16 / School District of Pattonville (after 1930) / Pattonville R-III (after 1951)
notes: IDENTITY AMBIGUITY: the 1907 two-room brick 'Pattonville Grade School' at 4020 Fee Fee Road (south of I-70) replaced the 1850 Fee Fee School and was expanded 1925-27; it served grades 1-8 until Pattonville High School opened in 1936, then K-6, and appears as 'Pattonville Grade School' on the district's 1956 elementary list. The district history separately lists 'Pattonville Elementary School (opened 1954)' as one of three schools closed in 1978 and sold in June 1981 — the grade school building 'later became the Vantage Credit Union.' The most coherent reading is that the grade school was renamed/replaced as Pattonville Elementary in ~1954 (which would explain the seed's 'closed 1950s'), but the district source never says so explicitly, so the 1978 closure is recorded as probable. This row may warrant merging with a future 'Pattonville Elementary School' row if another batch produces one. Students dispersed to remaining Pattonville elementaries after 1978.

name: Bridgeton Elementary School
notes: Seed's 'closed 1960s' corrected to 1978. District history: Bridgeton Elementary opened in 1953 as a two-story eight-classroom building on 3 acres at 11623 Natural Bridge Road in Bridgeton (two rooms, office and storage added 1956); it was one of three schools closed in 1978 for declining enrollment, and the board approved its sale to the First Korean Presbyterian Church of St. Louis in May 1985. Context: the Bridgeton school district was annexed into Pattonville during the 1949-50 school year — so the 1953 building was constructed under Pattonville; whether an older Bridgeton town-school building served in the interim (the Bridgeton Academy/Moravian School lineage reaches back to 1806) is unresolved and is the likely source of the seed's 'Bridgeton School' alias. Successor: none single; students dispersed to remaining Pattonville elementaries.

name: St. Ann Elementary School
district_operator: St Ann School District / Pattonville R-III
notes: District history gives no establishment date — 'records indicated it existed as early as 1956' (it appears on the 1956 list of five Pattonville elementaries, at Ashby Road south of St. Charles Rock Road; the detailed entry gives the address 3721 St. Bridget Lane, St. Ann). The board voted to close the school effective the 1982-83 school year under the K-5/middle-school reorganization, and in September 1982 the sole sale bid came from Hope Lutheran Church. Seed's unknown/unknown partially resolved (close year only). Physical ZIP is 63074, not 63043.

name: Willow Brook Elementary School
notes: Seed's 1959 confirmed: opened fall 1959 with Vernon Boddy as first principal, built in the Willow Brook subdivision at 11022 Schuetz Road, Creve Coeur. Still operating — listed on the district's current schools page and NCES. Actual ZIP is 63146, not 63043.

name: Bridgeway Elementary School
notes: Seed's 1963 confirmed: opened fall 1963 at 11635 Oakbury Court, Bridgeton, with Howard Graves as first principal; named for the Bridgeway subdivision. Still operating — listed on the district's current schools page and NCES. Actual ZIP is 63044, not 63043.

name: Briar Crest Elementary School
notes: Seed's 'closed 2018' corrected to 2013. District history: built 1964-65 with funds from a Jan. 26, 1965 bond issue; opened fall 1965 and dedicated Dec. 6, 1965, at 2900 Adie Road, St. Ann; first principal Nelson Smith; name from a school-naming contest. The school closed in 2013 due to budget cuts and was leased to a private school and the YWCA, then reopened in August 2018 as the Pattonville Early Childhood Center (Dr. Mary Krekeler, first director of early childhood) — so 2018 is the reuse date, not a closure. The building also housed the first Pattonville school breakfast program (1985). No successor school; the building continues in district use. Actual ZIP is 63074.

name: Carrollton Oaks Elementary School
notes: Seed's 'closed 2002' corrected to 2001. District history: opened September 1967 with 18 classrooms at 4385 Holmford, Bridgeton (6.5 acres adjacent to the Carrollton Oaks subdivision), built to relieve overcrowding at Carrollton, Bridgeton, Remington, Bridgeway and Pattonville elementaries; dedicated Jan. 8, 1968; first principal James Edwards. One of two Pattonville schools closed in 2001 for the Lambert-St. Louis International Airport expansion (new runway); the building was torn down after closure. Successor confirmed as Drummond Elementary School — built with airport funds as the replacement for both Carrollton and Carrollton Oaks elementaries; closing principal Jim Schwab became Drummond's principal. Drummond Elementary has no row in the seed dataset, so successor_school_id is 'unknown'; it is a current Pattonville elementary in Bridgeton (63044). NOTE: a separate seed row 'Carrollton Elementary School' (ALL-180, different batch) is the *other* school closed by the same 2001 airport expansion — do not conflate the two.
